chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When a man sneezes, respond to his sneeze by saying

key_terms.فَسَمِّتُوهُ: so name (Allah) for him / respond to his sneeze

ai.seo_question: What is the proper response when someone sneezes according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the Sunnah of responding to a sneeze with 'Yarhamuk Allah' (May Allah have mercy on you), highlighting the social bond of brotherhood in Islam. The specific mention of distance ('behind an island' or 'across the sea') underscores the universality and immediacy of this etiquette, regardless of physical proximity or the listener's ability to see the sneezer. This practice reflects the broader Islamic emphasis on maintaining communal ties and acknowledging divine blessings in daily interactions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When the man sneezes, so Name (Allah<sup>azwj</sup> respond to his sneeze) for him, and even if he was behind an island’. And in another report, ‘And even if he was behind the sea’’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘You should respond to one’s sneezing even if he is behind the island. In another Hadith it is said, ‘Even if it (response) is from behind the ocean.’”
